# Documentation Guidelines

## Code Documentation

- Document all public classes, methods, and functions with clear descriptions
- Use Dart's documentation comment format with triple slashes (`///`)
- Include parameter descriptions and return value information
- Provide usage examples for complex APIs or functions
- Document side effects, exceptions, and important behavioral notes

## README Standards

- Maintain a comprehensive README.md with project overview
- Include setup and installation instructions
- Document available scripts and development commands
- Provide deployment instructions for GitHub Pages
- Include contribution guidelines and coding standards

## API Documentation

- Document all public interfaces and their contracts
- Include endpoint descriptions, parameters, and response formats
- Provide example requests and responses
- Document error codes and handling procedures
- Maintain version compatibility information

## Architecture Documentation

- Document the overall application structure and design patterns
- Explain component organization and data flow
- Describe third-party integrations and dependencies
- Include diagrams for complex systems or workflows
- Document decision rationale for architectural choices

## User Documentation

- Create user guides for complex features or workflows
- Include screenshots and step-by-step instructions
- Document known limitations or browser compatibility issues
- Provide troubleshooting guides for common problems
- Maintain changelog for version updates and bug fixes

## Documentation Maintenance

- Keep documentation synchronized with code changes
- Review documentation during code reviews
- Use consistent formatting and style across all documents
- Link related documentation and cross-reference when helpful
- Regular audits to identify outdated or missing documentation
